newsitem.title: FRANCE: France denies baulking at new NATO raid in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: France denies baulking at new NATO raid in Bosnia.

text.p: France on Wednesday denied a report by the New York Times that it had declined to support plans for a second raid to capture high-ranking Bosnian Serbs suspected of war crimes.
"This information has no basis," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a routine news briefing, saying France was a strong supporter of bringing all war crimes suspects to justice.
The New York Times said Paris withheld its support for a new operation because it reckoned it too risky.
The daily quoted U.S. officials as saying that NATO planned more raids to follow up last week's operation against two Serbs indicted for war crimes. One man was arrested and a second shot dead.
Rummelhardt said the main responsibility for seizing suspects lay with the local authorities.
He also said French troops in the 31,000-strong NATO-led force "obey the rules of engagement set by NATO and follow the instructions of the force commander".
"We have always insisted on the need for suspects indicted by the war crimes tribunal to be arrested and transferred to this tribunal in The Hague," Rummelhardt said.

The New York Times said the U.S. government has been pressing NATO to seize prominent Bosnian Serbs charged with war crimes, many of whom live near Pale, the bastion of leading ultra-nationalists in Bosnian Serb territory.

It said that Paris was not opposed to the arrest of top Bosnian Serbs charged with war crimes but that the French felt the plan currently under consideration was too risky, according to American and French officials.
